artworks.title: Medusa
artworks.description: Painted in oil on a convex poplar shield mounted on a wooden frame, this celebrated tournament-piece freezes the very instant of Medusa's decapitation. Blood still spurts from the severed neck while the face, mouth agape in a final scream and crowned with writhing serpents, registers the horror of its own death. Caravaggio is said to have used his own features for the Gorgon's. Commissioned by Cardinal Francesco Maria del Monte as a gift for Ferdinando I de' Medici, the shield-shape turns the viewer into a Perseus safely beholding the monster's reflection. It is held in the Uffizi Gallery, Florence.

artworks.title: Perseus with the Head of Medusa
artworks.description: A bronze masterpiece of Florentine Mannerism, Cellini's statue shows the victorious Perseus standing astride Medusa's collapsed body, raising her severed head aloft as twisting locks of serpents and rivulets of bronze blood pour from both head and trunk. Commissioned by Duke Cosimo I de' Medici, it was cast in a single dramatic pour and unveiled in 1554 beneath the Loggia dei Lanzi on the Piazza della Signoria, Florence, where it still stands as a pointed dynastic emblem of the Medici triumphing over their enemies.

artworks.title: Medusa
artworks.description: The Swiss Symbolist Arnold Böcklin renders the Gorgon as a disembodied, masklike head, her serpent hair coiling outward and her eyes wide with a terror that seems to belong as much to the viewer as to the doomed creature. Stripped of any narrative of Perseus, the image isolates the apotropaic Gorgoneion itself—the petrifying gaze that turns onlookers to stone—and treats it as a study in dread and fascination, in keeping with the nineteenth-century Symbolist obsession with the femme fatale and the monstrous feminine.

artworks.title: Perseus beheading Medusa (Boeotian relief pithos)
artworks.description: On this Archaic Boeotian relief storage jar (pithos), one of the earliest surviving depictions of the myth, Perseus turns his face away as he plunges his blade into a Medusa whose form is rendered as a hybrid creature with the body of a centaur—an early, fluid iconography before the canonical winged, serpent-haired Gorgon was fixed. The molded relief decoration captures the decisive moment of the beheading from which Pegasus and Chrysaor would spring. It is preserved in the Musée du Louvre, Paris (inv. CA 795).

artifacts.title: Rondanini Medusa
artifacts.period: Roman marble copy after a Greek original of the 5th century BC
artifacts.description: The Gorgon's face made classically beautiful — calm, symmetrical, winged, with snakes knotted beneath the chin. The type is often connected with the gorgoneion on Phidias' Athena; this copy, named for the Palazzo Rondanini in Rome where Goethe admired it, defined the 'beautiful Medusa' for the modern imagination.

films.title: Clash of the Titans
films.description: Ray Harryhausen's stop-motion Medusa — a rattling, serpent-bodied archer stalking a temple of shadows — became the modern template for the Gorgon and one of the most celebrated monster sequences in cinema.

films.title: Clash of the Titans
films.description: Leterrier's CGI remake restages the temple duel for a new century — Medusa's gaze as blockbuster set-piece in Perseus' quest.

films.title: Percy Jackson & the Olympians: The Lightning Thief
films.description: Columbus' YA adaptation keeps Medusa's garden as a roadside trap — the Gorgon's kitsch statue-yard turning demigods to stone for a multiplex audience.

popCulture.title: Versace
popCulture.creator: Gianni Versace
popCulture.description: The Milanese fashion house took the Gorgon's head as its emblem — beauty that stops the beholder in their tracks — making Medusa one of the few ancient faces worn daily as a global logo.

popCulture.title: Kid Icarus
popCulture.creator: Nintendo
popCulture.description: Nintendo made Medusa the final boss of Angel Land — the Gorgon as the usurping goddess Pit must topple to free Palutena.

popCulture.title: Percy Jackson & the Olympians
popCulture.creator: Rick Riordan
popCulture.description: Riordan's demigod series restages Medusa as Auntie Em's garden-statuary shop — the Gorgon as a roadside American nightmare for middle-grade readers.

music.title: Persée
music.description: Lully's tragédie en musique for Louis XIV stages the Gorgon's beheading as court spectacle — Medusa as the monster Perseus must face before Andromeda.
